title: The Otters and the Wolf
author: Ellen C. Babbitt
summary: 两只水獭为分鱼争吵，狼借调解之名叼走了鱼身。
publicDomainBasis: Retold by Ellen C. Babbitt and published in 1922 by The Century Co. (pre-1923, public domain in the United States); Project Gutenberg releases it as public domain.

paragraphs.en: One day a Wolf said to her mate, "A longing has come upon me to eat fresh fish."
paragraphs.zh: 有一天，一只母狼对伴侣说：“我突然很想吃新鲜的鱼。”

paragraphs.en: "I will go and get some for you," said he and he went down to the river.
paragraphs.zh: “我去给你弄些来。”公狼说完，便往河边去了。

paragraphs.en: There he saw two Otters standing on the bank looking for fish. Soon one of the Otters saw a great fish, and entering the water with a bound, he caught hold of the tail of the fish.
paragraphs.zh: 他看见两只水獭站在岸上找鱼。不一会儿，一只水獭看见一条大鱼，纵身跳进水里，抓住了鱼的尾巴。

paragraphs.en: But the fish was strong and swam away, dragging the Otter after him. "Come and help me," the Otter called back to his friend. "This great fish will be enough for both of us!"
paragraphs.zh: 可那鱼力气很大，游走了，把水獭拖在后面。“快来帮我，”水獭朝朋友喊道，“这条大鱼够咱们俩吃了！”

paragraphs.en: So the other Otter went into the water. The two together were able to bring the fish to land. "Let us divide the fish into two parts."
paragraphs.zh: 于是另一只水獭也下了水。两只合力把鱼拖上了岸。“我们把鱼分成两半吧。”

paragraphs.en: "I want the half with the head on," said one.
paragraphs.zh: “我要带脑袋的那一半。”一只说。

paragraphs.en: "You cannot have that half. That is mine," said the other. "You take the tail."
paragraphs.zh: “那一半不能给你，那是我的，”另一只说，“你拿尾巴。”

paragraphs.en: The Wolf heard the Otters and he went up to them.
paragraphs.zh: 狼听见水獭的争吵，便走了过去。

paragraphs.en: Seeing the Wolf, the Otters said: "Lord of the gray-grass color, this fish was caught by both of us together. We cannot agree about dividing him. Will you divide him for us?"
paragraphs.zh: 水獭看见狼，说：“灰草色的大王，这鱼是我们两个一起捉到的。我们分不均匀。你替我们分吧？”

paragraphs.en: The Wolf cut off the tail and gave it to one, giving the head to the other. He took the large middle part for himself, saying to them, "You can eat the head and the tail without quarreling." And away he ran with the body of the fish. The Otters stood and looked at each other. They had nothing to say, but each thought to himself that the Wolf had run off with the best of the fish.
paragraphs.zh: 狼切下尾巴给了一只，把脑袋给了另一只，自己拿走了中间一大块，对他们说：“你们可以吃头和尾，就不用吵了。”说完，他带着鱼身子跑了。两只水獭站在那里互相看着，什么话也说不出来，可各自心里都明白，狼把最好的一块拿跑了。

paragraphs.en: The Wolf was pleased and said to himself, as he ran toward home, "Now I have fresh fish for my mate."
paragraphs.zh: 狼很得意，一边往家跑一边自言自语：“这下我给伴侣弄到鲜鱼了。”

paragraphs.en: His mate, seeing him coming, came to meet him, saying: "How did you get fish? You live on land, not in the water."
paragraphs.zh: 母狼看见他回来，迎上去说：“你怎么弄到鱼的？你住在陆地上，又不住在水里。”

paragraphs.en: Then he told her of the quarrel of the Otters. "I took the fish as pay for settling their quarrel," said he.
paragraphs.zh: 于是他把水獭争吵的事讲给她听。“我替他们调解争端，这鱼就是报酬。”他说。
